title: [BUG] (v3.2.0) `_cat/nodes` API shows negative values in cpu stats
body:
### Describe the bug

I ran into the below issue in 3.2.0 version that cpu usages could be negative and the same value (-1)

```
$ curl "https://<redacted-host>/_cat/nodes?v" -ku admin:test

ip             heap.percent ram.percent cpu load_1m load_5m load_15m node.role node.roles      cluster_manager name
10.251.175.203           38          60  -1    0.44    0.41     0.49 m         cluster_manager *               dev-opensearch-test-250821-master-1
10.251.117.144           20          60  -1    0.58    0.54     0.60 m         cluster_manager -               dev-opensearch-test-250821-master-0
10.251.225.190           67          90  -1    1.79    1.14     1.03 di        data,ingest     -               dev-opensearch-test-250821-data-0
10.251.143.196           24          60  -1    0.40    0.68     0.61 m         cluster_manager -               dev-opensearch-test-250821-master-2
```

### Related component

Clients

### To Reproduce

1. deploy opensearch cluster using 3.2.0 version
2. After your cluster runs successfully, `curl "https://<redacted-host>/_cat/nodes?v" -ku admin:test`
3. It also happens wrongly when you try `_cluster/stats` API

### Expected behavior

.

### Additional Details

**Plugins**
I just added the prometheus-exporter plugin by building new Docker image
```
FROM <redacted-host>/library/opensearchproject/opensearch:3.2.0

COPY prometheus-exporter-3.2.0.0.zip /tmp/
RUN ./bin/opensearch-plugin install file:/tmp/prometheus-exporter-3.2.0.0.zip
```

**Host/Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: All hosts are worker nodes of kubernetes v1.31.4 and based on RHEL 8.10 (4.18.0 kernel)
 - Version: OpenSearch 3.2.0

**Additional context**
- Air-gapped environment but I believe it doesn't matter with this issue.

I'm not able to reproduce this on Ubuntu 24.04.3 running the tarball or the docker image. In all cases I get non-negative value.

Here is the code in question:

https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/blob/631bed420a92e0e44cf15e26e89184146be67258/server/src/main/java/org/opensearch/monitor/os/OsProbe.java#L239-L241

To summarize, it uses reflection to invoke `com.sun.management.OperatingSystemMXBean#getCpuLoad`. It does have a couple fallback paths to return -1 in case that class or method is not available at runtime.

@participant15 I believe you have some experience in this area. Any idea what might be going on here?

comments.body: The method used [here](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/blob/631bed420a92e0e44cf15e26e89184146be67258/server/src/main/java/org/opensearch/monitor/os/OsProbe.java#L97) was changed from `getSystemCpuLoad` to `getCpuLoad` in PR #18322. @participant11 do you have additional context on this particular change?

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
To answer my own question, `getSystemCpuLoad` has been deprecated since Java 14 in favor of `getCpuLoad`, but the [implementation requirements](https://<redacted-host>/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/jdk.management/com/sun/management/OperatingSystemMXBean.html#getSystemCpuLoad()) state that the methods must return the same value.

@participant4 So your test Java app using the OpenSearch utiilities is able to return the correct values? However, OpenSearch itself is running under systemd. We have recently updated the [systemd configuration](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/blob/646f937f886c58eccbb45b96a97df9ca1305ecf5/distribution/packages/src/common/systemd/opensearch.service) to improve the security posture. @participant16 @participant7 could that systemd configuration be the issue here?

comments.author: participant5

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
I have not found an environment where I can reproduce this to get to a definitive cause. The leading theory I have is that in some environments the JDK is attempting to read `/proc/stat` and that is being blocked by the systemd configuration. The main datapoint supporting that is that @participant4 wrote a test Java program using the OpenSearch utilities that was able to get a valid CPU value, but the OpenSearch process is returning -1.

For anyone following along that is seeing this error, one test you can do is replace

```
ReadOnlyPaths=/proc/self/mountinfo /proc/diskstats
```

with

```
ReadOnlyPaths=/proc/self/mountinfo /proc/diskstats /proc/stat
```

in the systemd configuration to add permissions to read /proc/stat. On my Ubuntu test machine this file was located at `/usr/lib/systemd/system/opensearch.service`.

I'll have to compile a list of Github issues I've seen with JDK >= 24. Basically the JDK has been removing a bunch of internal calls to AccessController.doPrivileged and it may manifest as these errors.

IMO The solution is to put these grants generically in the security.policy file which essentially mimics JDK behavior where the access is implicit and does not need to be explicitly granted.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
@participant8 @participant10 @participant5  Spent some time looking into the issue, there are two things to mention:
 - the way OpenSearch fetches CPU stats (for CPU load in particular), is using `<redacted-host>.OperatingSystemImpl::getCpuLoad`
 - the `OperatingSystemImpl::getCpuLoad` may return -1 if perf counters are disabled fe (or any other reason), this is documented https://<redacted-host>/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/jdk.management/com/sun/management/OperatingSystemMXBean.html#getCpuLoad()

So in general, -1 is (unfortunately) the value we could get. Now, the solution(s) to it:
 - on bootstrap, we could do a check to report such issue earlier (but do not fail the bootstrap procedure)
 - document that on some systems JVM may not report getCpuLoad() correctly, so `-1` will be returned
 - also, we don't log any exception in this case, we could do this once on bootstrap only

Thoughts? Thanks folks!

However, the OpenSearch API `/_nodes/_local/stats/os` is still reporting `"percent" : -1`. Since the underlying JVM OperatingSystemMXBean is clearly able to read the CPU load without failing, is it possible that OpenSearch's OS stats probe is explicitly converting 0.0 (or extremely low values) to -1, or perhaps catching a different silent exception when it polls these metrics? If the assumption is ok, is it possible to do a "warm-up call": during the initialization phase of the OpenSearch node (specifically within its OS stats probe or metrics service), it should make a single and discarded "dummy" call to getCpuLoad() in order to establish the initial baseline for the JVM, ensuring that the first actual metric scrape by Prometheus or a user receives a valid calculation based on a defined time period.
